title: Malerkotla, 1872
hookLine: Namdharis taken prisoner after a raid were executed by cannon on the order of British officials, without trial

cards: A heavy day, so here is where it goes before it starts. Malerkotla is a small town in the Punjab, the seat of a princely state.
Near it, Namdhari prisoners were tied to the mouths of cannon by order of a British official, and the guns were fired. There was no trial.
Namdharis remember these men as shaheeds, martyrs, and they gather at Malerkotla to remember them still. Today isn't about the details of the killing. It's about how a community remembers.

teach.h: A RAID, AND DEATHS ON BOTH SIDES.
teach.b: First, what led to it. Some Namdharis were angered by the killing of cows, and a band of them attacked Malerkotla. There was fighting, and people of the town were killed as well as Namdharis.
Namdhari histories say Baba Ram Singh had not sent them, and had tried to hold his followers back. Second, the response.
The British official in charge of the district had the captured men executed by cannon, without a trial. A senior official approved more executions the next day.
Even the British government found this too far, and the official was removed from his post.
Third, a story Namdharis tell. Among the prisoners, they say, was a young boy. The official offered to spare him if he would deny his teacher.
The boy refused, and was cut down. This is the community's memory, told and retold, rather than a court record. Fourth, why it's remembered.
The daily Ardas, the prayer Sikhs stand for, calls to mind those who gave their lives and kept their faith, and it ends by asking for the good of all, sarbat da bhala.
Remembering, in that prayer, is not revenge.
At Malerkotla, the town's own people were caught in the violence too, and this lesson keeps the same silence for their dead.
That's the shape of today's line: saying the names, not letting them disappear, and not turning grief into a weapon.

how: Namdhari Sikhs gather at Malerkotla to remember the Namdharis executed there by cannon as martyrs, and the Sikh Ardas calls to mind those who kept their faith to the end.

games.q: a community has lost its people to a terrible killing. how does it remember them?
o: it forgets, so the pain will fade.
it says their names and keeps silence, without turning grief into revenge.
games.why: Namdharis gather at Malerkotla to remember their shaheeds, and the Ardas recalls those who kept faith and ends by asking for the good of all.

practice: For the first minute, breathe slowly and let the week settle: Lavan, a loss remembered, something found again, two reformers.

Then keep one minute of silence for those who died at Malerkotla, the prisoners and the townspeople alike. If you pray, stay with Waheguru in the quiet; if you don't, let the silence say they mattered.
